blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, British humour is less a personality feature and more a signal — a precise one. A senior leader who makes a dry, self-deprecating joke at the start of a tense meeting is saying several things at once: "I am not threatened by this room", "we are all adults here", and "we can afford to handle this with some lightness". The joke does work that a paragraph of warmth could not.

Equally, a pointed understatement from a senior colleague — "that was perhaps slightly less than ideal" — after a serious failure is often the most severe public criticism that the British system allows. The softness of the language is inversely proportional to the seriousness of the message.

For newcomers to British executive rooms, the danger is to miss the signal entirely. The CEO who smiles and says "bit of a mess, then" is not relaxed — they are telegraphing that something must change, quickly, while giving the person responsible a dignified way to understand without being publicly cornered. That is leadership, in a British accent.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level British humour is best understood as…
items.why: "British humour is less a personality feature and more a signal — a precise one."

items.q: What is the stated relationship between the softness of the language and the seriousness of the message?
options: Softer language means a trivial message
items.why: "The softness of the language is inversely proportional to the seriousness of the message."

items.q: When the CEO smiles and says "bit of a mess, then", the author suggests he is…
options: signalling that something must change quickly
avoiding the subject to spare feelings
items.why: "is not relaxed — they are telegraphing that something must change, quickly."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Executives joke mainly to make meetings feel casual.
A light remark at the top can be a serious instruction.
Understatement can carry more weight than blunt criticism.
A dry joke signals confidence rather than fear.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que o humor executivo é sinalização precisa, não uma tentativa de deixar a reunião casual.

items.q: The phrase "without being publicly cornered" suggests that British executive humour also serves to…
options: let the responsible person save face while getting the message
reward the person for the poor result
hide the mistake from the rest of the board
items.why: Inferência: o humor entrega a crítica preservando a dignidade de quem errou — uma saída sem humilhação pública.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver explicando a um recém-chegado o que o CEO quis dizer. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me translate that for you, because I could see the look on your face. When the CEO smiled and said "bit of a mess, then", you thought he was letting us off lightly. He was doing precisely the opposite.

In a British boardroom, that is about as severe as it gets in public. We missed the quarter by a mile, and everybody in the room knew it. Had he raised his voice or read out the numbers line by line, he would have cornered the division head in front of twenty people — and nobody would have learned anything. Instead, he handed her the message wrapped in six understated words.

The trick, and it is a trick, is to hear the weight underneath the lightness. "Bit of a mess" is not a shrug; it is an instruction. Fix it, fix it fast, and do not make me say it again. If you had laughed along as though it were a genuine joke, you would have shown the whole room that you cannot read it — and that costs you far more here than one bad quarter ever would.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the newcomer initially think the CEO's remark meant?
options: That the CEO had not seen the results
That the CEO wanted the numbers read aloud
That the CEO was about to resign
That the CEO was letting the team off lightly
items.why: "you thought he was letting us off lightly. He was doing precisely the opposite."

items.q: According to Oliver, why did the CEO avoid raising his voice or reading out the numbers?
options: He wanted to end the meeting quickly
It would have cornered the division head in front of everyone
He was not sure the numbers were correct
He had not prepared the figures
items.why: "he would have cornered the division head in front of twenty people — and nobody would have learned anything."

items.q: Oliver says "Bit of a mess" is not a shrug; it is…
items.why: "it is an instruction. Fix it, fix it fast."

items.q: Oliver implies that laughing along as though it were a genuine joke would have…
options: revealed that you cannot read the signal
ended the meeting on a good note
shown you belong to the in-group
items.why: Inferência: rir do comentário como piada real exporia que você não decodifica o sinal — falha maior que o trimestre ruim.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "that costs you far more here than one bad quarter ever would"?
options: One bad quarter always ends a career
Being seen as unable to read the room damages you more than a bad result
The company fines people for laughing
items.why: Inferência: não saber ler o sinal social pesa mais, a longo prazo, do que um único resultado financeiro fraco.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A dry, self-deprecating joke told the room he was not threatened." Self-deprecating means…
options: belittling oneself, often to disarm others
items.why: Self-deprecating = autodepreciativo: fazer piada de si mesmo, aqui para desarmar a tensão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The CEO was quietly ___ that a change was needed, without saying it directly."
items.why: To telegraph = sinalizar/telegrafar uma mensagem de forma indireta mas legível.

items.q: "He gave her a dignified way to understand." Dignified here means…
items.why: Dignified = digno: um modo que preserva o respeito da pessoa, sem humilhação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Reading the joke wrong left him feeling ___ in front of the whole board."
items.why: Cornered = encurralado: sem saída, exposto publicamente.

items.q: "He could afford to handle it with some lightness." Lightness means…
items.why: Lightness = leveza: um tom ameno, não pesado, ao tratar de um assunto tenso.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em salas executivas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Only the CEO can sign off on the recovery plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The division head knew she had to follow through after that remark." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado ou cobrado.

items.q: "A newcomer might read too much into a friendly smile." To read too much into means to…
options: interpret more meaning than is there
items.why: Read too much into = enxergar significado onde não há tanto — o erro oposto ao de perder o sinal.

items.q: "Understating it let him get the message across without a scene." To get the message across means to…
items.why: Get the message across = conseguir transmitir a mensagem de forma compreendida.

items.q: "Laughing at the wrong moment can rub people the wrong way in the boardroom." This means to…
items.why: Rub someone the wrong way = irritar/desagradar alguém sem querer.
